headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make n8n→Prefect pair vulnerable to data leakage and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and orchestrate tools as sub-nodes, while Prefect exposes workflow metadata and broad egress. If n8n passes attacker-controlled file or workflow content into Prefect-managed steps, prompt-like content can steer downstream automation. The shared path is plausible, but not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF n8n writes untrusted content to a shared file or datastore that Prefect later reads as instructions
IF Prefect workflows ingest n8n-produced text without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from n8n to Prefect
Insert a manual review step before any text is re-used as instructions
Store untrusted payloads separately from control metadata
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress, filesystem access, and handles per-credential secrets; Prefect also has broad egress and touches workflow metadata. If they share a workspace or connected system, sensitive workflow data can flow from n8n into Prefect outputs or external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or connected datastore
IF n8n workflow inputs include secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials between the two systems
Disable unnecessary outbound integrations in both agents
Mask secrets before handing data from n8n to Prefect
Review logs for accidental payload capture
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Prefect is an orchestration system that may also mutate shared workflow state. The profiles do not show explicit locking or a shared mutable resource, but if both touch the same directory or datastore, write conflicts and race conditions are plausible in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, database, or artifact store
IF orchestration runs them concurrently without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Add a lock around shared mutable resources
Run one agent at a time for shared targets
Check for overlapping write paths before execution
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools, and Prefect is an automation/orchestration platform; that makes it plausible for n8n output to become Prefect input and trigger downstream actions. If Prefect treats n8n-produced text or metadata as authoritative, a bad upstream result can cascade into irreversible workflow actions. The interaction is not documented, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes n8n-generated outputs without verification
IF those outputs drive API calls, deployments, or scheduled jobs
mitigations: Require schema validation on all n8n outputs before Prefect uses them
Add a human approval gate for action-taking workflows
Log and diff upstream outputs before execution
Disable automatic retries on malformed upstream data
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between systems

E_compliance.rationale: n8n explicitly handles per-credential secrets and whatever the workflow processes, while Prefect touches workflow metadata. If regulated data is routed through n8n and then into Prefect logs or metadata, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions or certifications, so the compliance risk is real but not provably high.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are included in workflow payloads
IF Prefect retains metadata longer than the source system's policy
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between systems
Redact secrets from workflow metadata
Set short retention on logs and run outputs
Confirm residency and DPA coverage for each integration
requires-engineering: align retention policies across both systems
